sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日商业与政策通讯

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《DealBook》的商业和政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine

sentences.zh: 其中包括 J·D·万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经删减的实时对话。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, I was supposed to be traveling back home from a work trip in
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，我本该结束在明尼阿波利斯

sentences.en: Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 的一次工作旅行，启程回家。

sentences.en: Five minutes before my Uber arrived, I was scrolling through my emails and I saw the headline, your flight was canceled.
sentences.zh: 就在我的优步到达前五分钟，我正翻看着电子邮件，突然看到一条标题：“您的航班已取消”。

sentences.en: Here's your new itinerary.
sentences.zh: “以下是您的新行程。”

sentences.en: No reason given.
sentences.zh: 没有给出任何原因。

sentences.en: Oh, well.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I was like, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，随它去吧。

sentences.en: At least I still have a flight, right?
sentences.zh: 至少我还有航班，对吧？

sentences.en: While I was waiting at the gate, I get another email from Delta and my flight to Cincinnati was delayed.
sentences.zh: 当我正在登机口等待时，我又收到了一封来自达美航空的邮件，说我飞往辛辛那提的航班延误了。

sentences.en: Again, no reason given.
sentences.zh: 同样，没有给出任何原因。

sentences.en: And now I'm really confused because I'm like, wait a minute, how do I catch my flight in Cincinnati at
sentences.zh: 现在我真的糊涂了，因为我在想，等一下，

sentences.en: 4.59 if I don't get there until 5.12?
sentences.zh: 如果我5点12分才到，怎么赶得上4点59分飞往辛辛那提的航班？

sentences.en: You know, am I going to time travel?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，难道我要进行时间旅行吗？

sentences.en: And I chose to reroute my flight through Raleigh, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我选择将航班改道北卡罗来纳州罗利。

sentences.en: We're on the flight.
sentences.zh: 我们登上了飞机。

sentences.en: I'm finally going somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我总算要出发了。

sentences.en: We land in
sentences.zh: 我们在罗利降落，

sentences.en: Raleigh and I start getting all the notifications I miss.
sentences.zh: 我开始收到所有错过的通知。

sentences.en: And among them, I see another headline from
sentences.zh: 在这些通知中，我看到了达美航空的另一个

sentences.en: Delta.
sentences.zh: 标题。

sentences.en: Your flight was canceled.
sentences.zh: “您的航班已取消。”

sentences.en: Here's your new itinerary.
sentences.zh: “以下是您的新行程。”

sentences.en: So I deboard and I head to the Delta desk.
sentences.zh: 于是我下了飞机，径直走向达美航空的服务台。

sentences.en: And they say that the flight from Raleigh to New York was canceled due to inclement weather and that there's nothing they can do.
sentences.zh: 他们说，由于恶劣天气，从罗利飞往纽约的航班被取消了，他们对此无能为力。

sentences.en: This is really the first indication all day after two canceled flights and a delay that I actually have a reason why a flight was canceled.
sentences.zh: 这是整整一天里，在经历了两架航班取消和一次延误之后，我得到的关于航班为什么被取消的第一个确切原因。

sentences.en: It's an act of God.
sentences.zh: 这是不可抗力。

sentences.en: They blamed God.
sentences.zh: 他们把责任怪到了上帝头上。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》播客。

sentences.en: My name's Dana.
sentences.zh: 我叫达娜。

sentences.en: I live in Charlotte, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我住在北卡罗来纳州夏洛特。

sentences.en: My name is James Mason.
sentences.zh: 我叫詹姆斯·梅森。

sentences.en: My name is Sam.
sentences.zh: 我叫萨姆。

sentences.en: My name is Gwen.
sentences.zh: 我叫格温。

sentences.en: Across the country this summer.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，在全国各地。

sentences.en: I show up to the airport and they're like, oh no, your flight is canceled.
sentences.zh: 我赶到机场，他们却说：“哦，不，您的航班取消了。”

sentences.en: The flight's canceled.
sentences.zh: 航班取消了。

sentences.en: My flight is canceled.
sentences.zh: 我的航班取消了。

sentences.en: Airline travel has been defined by new depths of inconvenience.
sentences.zh: 航空旅行遭遇了前所未有的极度不便。

sentences.en: And I get up to the front of this line and the employee says, we don't have a ticket for you.
sentences.zh: 当我排到队伍最前面时，工作人员说：“我们没有您的机票。”

sentences.en: And this plane is overbooked.
sentences.zh: “而且这架飞机超售了。”

sentences.en: It was like this anvil crashed on my head.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像一块铁砧砸在我头上。

sentences.en: Disruption.
sentences.zh: 混乱。

sentences.en: I was definitely going to miss the birthday dinner at that point.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，我肯定是赶不上生日晚宴了。

sentences.en: So I sent my girlfriend a few apologetic texts and waited.
sentences.zh: 所以我给女朋友发了几条道歉的短信，然后等待着。

sentences.en: Thankfully, my girlfriend was pretty understanding about the whole situation.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，我女朋友对整个情况还算理解。

sentences.en: And misery.
sentences.zh: 还有痛苦。

sentences.en: I got to this point of desperation where I realized it just settles on you.
sentences.zh: 我感到了绝望，意识到这种情绪会重重地压在你心头。

sentences.en: It feels so heavy when you're like, I'm not getting home.
sentences.zh: 当你觉得“我回不了家了”时，那种感觉太沉重了。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Neeraj Chakshi explains why two and a half years into the pandemic, flying remains such an unpleasant experience.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事尼拉杰·查克希将解释为什么在疫情爆发两年半后，飞行依然是一段如此糟糕的体验。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月17日，星期三。

sentences.en: Neeraj, by now it's a well-established fact that this is the summer of airline hell.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，现在大家普遍认为，这是航空地狱之夏。

sentences.en: And the testimonials from the daily listeners that we played at the top of the show really capture that.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目开头播放的《每日新闻》听众的亲身经历，完美地捕捉到了这一点。

sentences.en: The delays, the cancellations, and the maddening explanations for them.
sentences.zh: 航班延误、取消，以及那些令人抓狂的解释。

sentences.en: It is very bad.
sentences.zh: 情况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I hear from readers.
sentences.zh: 我从读者那里听到。

sentences.en: I hear from friends.
sentences.zh: 我从朋友那里听到。

sentences.en: I have nervously tried to avoid
sentences.zh: 我一直在小心翼翼地试图自己避开

sentences.en: problems myself, but it is really a summer of hell.
sentences.zh: 这些麻烦，但这真的是一个地狱般的夏天。

sentences.en: So we want to talk about the forces behind all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想聊聊这一切背后的原因。

sentences.en: How it can be that this long into the pandemic, when it feels like air travel really should be more or less back to normal, it's somehow gotten worse.
sentences.zh: 为什么在疫情持续了这么久之后，当人们觉得航空旅行真的应该多多少少恢复正常时，情况却不知怎么变得更糟了。

sentences.en: How did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: Well, to understand that, we have to go back to early 2020.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要理解这一点，我们得回到2020年初。

sentences.en: COVID was wreaking havoc across the economy.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情正在给整个经济造成浩劫。

sentences.en: For the airlines, it started in probably February 2020, where we really started to see international flights affected.
sentences.zh: 对航空公司来说，这一切大概始于2020年2月，当时我们真正开始看到国际航班受到影响。

sentences.en: And by April of 2020, more than 95% of air traffic has just disappeared.
sentences.zh: 到2020年4月，超过95%的航空客运量直接消失了。

sentences.en: To give you an idea, on March 1st, the TSA was screening about 2.3 million people per day.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个概念，在3月1日，美国运输安全管理局每天安检大约230万人。

sentences.en: By mid-April, that's down to fewer than 90,000 people.
sentences.zh: 到4月中旬，这一数字降至不到9万。人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So from there, the federal government decided to bail the industry out.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，联邦政府决定出手拯救航空业。

sentences.en: They give airlines about
sentences.zh: 他们向航空公司提供大约

sentences.en: $25 billion.
sentences.zh: 250亿美元。

sentences.en: And that's just to pay workers, just to keep people employed, to avoid mass layoffs and bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 这笔资金仅用于支付工人工资，仅仅为了让人们保持就业，以避免大规模裁员和破产。

sentences.en: And then they eventually increased that to $54 billion.
sentences.zh: 后来他们最终将金额增加到了540亿美元。

sentences.en: That helps, but the industry still has no sense of how long this is going to last, when traffic will recover.
sentences.zh: 这确实有帮助，但航空业仍然不知道这种情况会持续多久，客运量何时才能恢复。

sentences.en: We still didn't have vaccines.
sentences.zh: 当时我们还没有疫苗。

sentences.en: They didn't know what was coming next, so they decided to thin their ranks.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道接下来会发生什么，所以他们决定精简人员。

sentences.en: And so in the summer of 2020, they turned to their workers and they say, you know, we're willing to give you money
sentences.zh: 所以在2020年夏天，他们找到员工说，你知道的，我们愿意给你钱

sentences.en: to leave in the form of buyouts, in the form of early retirement packages, and tens of thousands of people take advantage of it.
sentences.zh: 让你离职，通过买断工龄、提前退休计划的形式，成千上万的人接受了这一点。

sentences.en: Ultimately, at its low point, the industry is about 12% smaller than it was just before the pandemic began.
sentences.zh: 最终，在行业的低谷期，其规模比疫情爆发前缩小了约12%。

sentences.en: And while we're all at home and not flying, that's not something we, as passengers at least, are really paying that much attention to, right?
sentences.zh: 当我们都呆在家里不坐飞机时，作为乘客的我们至少并没有真正太关注这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, what's happening in the airline industry is not top of mind at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时航空业发生的事情并不是我们最关心的头等大事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All this is going on behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都在幕后发生着。

sentences.en: And, you know, a lot of people probably aren't even noticing that this has gone down.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，很多人可能甚至没有注意到这一点已经发生了。

sentences.en: But that starts to change in early 2021.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在2021年初开始改变。

sentences.en: It's one of the more busy weeks airport officials can remember in a while.
sentences.zh: 这是机场官员记忆中一段时间以来最繁忙的几个星期之一。

sentences.en: Flights coming back, signaling the start of the return to normal.
sentences.zh: 航班回归，标志着生活恢复正常之旅的开始。

sentences.en: That spring, a lot of people start to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 那年春天，许多人开始接种疫苗。

sentences.en: They start to feel more comfortable traveling.
sentences.zh: 他们开始觉得出行更安心了。

sentences.en: Our last three weeks in America have been the three strongest weeks for bookings since the pandemic hit.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国的最后三周是自疫情爆发以来预订量最强劲的三周。

sentences.en: And each week has been stronger than the laSt.
sentences.zh: 而且每一周都比上一周更强劲。

sentences.en: We see the airline recovery really pick up steam that summer.
sentences.zh: 我们看到航空业的复苏在那个夏天真正开始全速前进。

sentences.en: But as it picks up steam, we also start to see some cracks forming.
sentences.zh: 但随着它全速前进，我们也开始看到一些裂痕正在形成。

sentences.en: Spirit Airlines scrubbed even more flights today after a series of cancellations and delays, but it's dating back to the weekend.
sentences.zh: 在经历了一系列取消和延误之后，边疆航空今天取消了更多的航班，但这些问题可以追溯到周末。

sentences.en: There are various weekend meltdowns for different airlines.
sentences.zh: 不同的航空公司都遭遇了各自的周末崩盘。

sentences.en: The budget airline reports it's trying to reboot operations now.
sentences.zh: 这家廉价航空公司报告称，目前正在尝试重启运营。

sentences.en: At one point, Spirit Airlines lost $50 million over a nearly two-week stretch because of various disruptions.
sentences.zh: 一度，由于各种混乱，边疆航空在将近两周的时间里损失了5000万美元。

sentences.en: Southwest Airlines says its recent meltdown cost the airline $75 million, and its plan to prevent similar incidents may impact your holiday travel plans.
sentences.zh: 西南航空表示，其最近的系统瘫痪让公司损失了7500万美元，而其防止类似事件再次发生的计划可能会影响你的假日旅行计划。

sentences.en: Later that fall of 2021, Southwest Airlines lost $75 million over a long weekend.
sentences.zh: 2021年那个秋天晚些时候，西南航空在一个长周末损失了7500万美元。

sentences.en: And then the Omicron waves started to develop just before the winter holidays.
sentences.zh: 接着，在寒假前夕，奥密克戎变异株疫情开始爆发。

sentences.en: Now those COVID numbers are causing flight cancellations across the country,
sentences.zh: 现在，这些新冠确诊数字导致全国各地的航班取消，

sentences.en: United and Delta canceling at least 100 each.
sentences.zh: 美联航和达美航空各自取消了至少100个航班。

sentences.en: And that started decimating staffing on the planes.
sentences.zh: 这开始急剧削减飞机上的机组人员。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember so many people had their holiday travel canceled because all these airline crews were getting COVID.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得很多人因为所有的这些机组人员都感染了新冠，导致他们的假日旅行被取消。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that really laid bare that there was a staffing issue here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真正暴露了这里存在着人员配备问题。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, the Omicron wave was really severe, but it also highlighted that, you know, the airlines don't have a lot of buffer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然奥密克戎疫情非常严重，但它也凸显出，你知道的，航空公司的缓冲余地并不多。

sentences.en: They're really operating on a razor's edge here.
sentences.zh: 他们在这里真的是在走钢丝。

sentences.en: And that was something that needed to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 这是需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: And to some extent, they were addressing it.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他们确实在解决这个问题。

sentences.en: They were hiring into winter, and they continued to hire.
sentences.zh: 他们在冬天期间一直在招人，并且还在继续招聘。

sentences.en: But I think it really made it clear to them that they needed to really accelerate those efforts, especially with the summer of 2022 coming up.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这让他们真正清楚地意识到，他们需要真正加速这些努力，特别是随着2022年夏天的临近。

sentences.en: So by the spring, the airlines have pretty big ambitions for the summer.
sentences.zh: 因此到了春季，航空公司对夏天有着相当大的野心。

sentences.en: It's always the busiest season of every year.
sentences.zh: 这历来是每年最繁忙的季节。

sentences.en: And there's a sense that people are getting really excited to travel too.
sentences.zh: 人们也有一种感觉，大家都对出行感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: You hear from airlines that this summer is going to be great.
sentences.zh: 你从航空公司那里听到的是，今年夏天将会非常棒。

sentences.en: This summer is going to see tons of traffic.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天将迎来大量的客流。

sentences.en: We're going to be back to normal.
sentences.zh: 我们将恢复正常。

sentences.en: In April of this year, the chief executive of United
sentences.zh: 今年4月，联合航空公司的

sentences.en: Airlines, Scott Kirby, said that the demand environment is the strongest that it's been in his 30 years in the industry.
sentences.zh: 首席执行官斯科特·柯比表示，当前的需求环境是他进入该行业30年来最强劲的。

sentences.en: And I think at that point, you start to wonder if demand is going to be back and airlines are still clearly a little nervous that they're going to be able to meet it.
sentences.zh: 我想在那时，你开始怀疑需求是否真的会恢复，而航空公司显然仍然有点担心他们是否有能力满足这种需求。

sentences.en: You know, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 你知道，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, we kind of know what happens.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们大致知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Things obviously do not go smoothly.
sentences.zh: 事情显然没有顺利进行。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Memorial Day weekend kicks off summer travel season, and it was okay.
sentences.zh: 阵亡将士纪念日周末拉开了夏季旅行季的序幕，当时还算可以。

sentences.en: But then we just start to see delays consistently throughout June and into July.
sentences.zh: 但随后我们在整个6月和7月开始持续看到航班延误。

sentences.en: Of all the attractions Michelle saw on her holiday in the UK, the floor of Terminal 5 was not on her list of places to spend a night.
sentences.zh: 在米歇尔在英国度假期间看到的所有景点中，5号航站楼的地板绝对不在她打算过夜的名单上。

sentences.en: It's just as clear that the industry can't get a hold on getting things right and running smoothly.
sentences.zh: 同样显而易见的是，航空业无法掌控局面，无法让事情步入正轨并顺利运行。

sentences.en: The chaos comes just as airports brace for another flood of travelers July 4th weekend
sentences.zh: 就在机场为7月4日独立日周末的又一波旅客潮做准备时，混乱便随之而来了，

sentences.en: and anticipated 11 million to pass through airports over the holiday, despite the soaring cost of travel.
sentences.zh: 预计在假日期间将有1100万人通过机场，尽管旅行成本在飙升。

sentences.en: You're seeing people have flights canceled and to get to where they're going, they have to pay thousands more than they were originally planning, especially if they're flying
sentences.zh: 你会看到人们的航班被取消，为了到达目的地，他们必须支付比原计划多出数千美元的费用，特别是如果他们

sentences.en: with family.
sentences.zh: 与家人一起

sentences.en: One traveler tweeting, I see London, I see Air France, but I don't see my underpants.
sentences.zh: 出行。

sentences.en: Because they're in my suitcase that you left at Paris, Charles de Gaulle Airport 11 days ago.
sentences.zh: 一位旅客发推特说：“我看到了伦敦，我看到了法航，但我没看到我的内裤。”

sentences.en: People who have plans, events to make miss them by sometimes days.
sentences.zh: “因为它们在我11天前落在巴黎戴高乐机场的手提箱里。”

sentences.en: And for a lot of people, this is their first big trip in two plus years, and it's being ruined.
sentences.zh: 有计划、有活动要赶的人有时会错过好几天。

sentences.en: So if you are thinking about traveling to Europe this summer, buckle up, because it is being described as Armageddon.
sentences.zh: 如果你正考虑今年夏天去欧洲旅游，系好安全带吧，因为这次的情况被形容为世界末日。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember the scenes, at least on TV, of people just freaking out over lost baggage.
sentences.zh: 对，我还记得那些场景，至少在电视上，人们因为行李丢失而彻底抓狂。

sentences.en: I remember
sentences.zh: 我记得

sentences.en: Heathrow in London just being a mess.
sentences.zh: 伦敦希思罗机场简直一片混乱。

sentences.en: I mean, it definitely seemed like things were falling apart in this really dramatic way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事情以一种非常戏剧化的方式分崩离析，这绝对是显而易见的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they were.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，它们确实如此。

sentences.en: And every summer is bad, but this summer clearly stood out.
sentences.zh: 而且每年夏天都很糟糕，但今年夏天显然格外突出。

sentences.en: And we start to really appreciate all these problems kind of coming together from earlier in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们开始真正意识到，疫情早期的所有这些问题现在都汇集到了一起。

sentences.en: And of those, the biggest is staffing.
sentences.zh: 而在这些问题中，最大的问题就是人手不足。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，而且不需要输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在该App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报App，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Neeraj, before the break, you said there are a few problems left over from COVID.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，在休息之前，你说过还有一些遗留的疫情问题。

sentences.en: COVID hangovers, if you will, that are conspiring to make our air travel miserable this summer, and that staffing is the biggest one.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，可以说是新冠后遗症，它们共同作用，让我们的今年夏天的航空旅行变得苦不堪言，而人手不足是其中最大的一个问题。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: There's sort of two flavors here.
sentences.zh: 这里大致有两种情况。

sentences.en: There's the people who you can hire back, but you're having trouble because this is just a really competitive job market, and it has been for more than a year.
sentences.zh: 一种是你可以重新雇佣的人，但你遇到了麻烦，因为这是一个竞争非常激烈的就业市场，而且这种情况已经持续了一年多。

sentences.en: Unemployment is at a 50-year low.
sentences.zh: 失业率处于50年来的最低点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just really hard to hire people, no matter what you're hiring them for.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无论你招募他们做什么，招人真的很难。

sentences.en: The other piece of this is something that is both current and longstanding, and that's the pilot and mechanic shortage.
sentences.zh: 这其中的另一个部分是既与当前相关又长期存在的问题，那就是飞行员和机修工的短缺。

sentences.en: For years, you've had this shortage looming, and suddenly airlines are really desperate to hire pilots and to build up their mechanics, and there just aren't any.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这种短缺一直隐隐逼近，突然之间，航空公司极其迫切地想要招募飞行员并建立他们的机修团队，但根本就没有人。

sentences.en: The military was a huge source of pilots for a long time, but the military has seen fewer pilots in recent years too, and so that pipeline has thinned out.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，军方一直是飞行员的一个巨大来源，但近年来军方的飞行员也变少了，因此这一人才输送渠道已经变窄了。

sentences.en: The other problem is that in the 2000s, the industry went through a lot of bankruptcies, and in that process, pilots lost some benefits, the job
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，在2000年代，航空业经历了一系列破产，在这个过程中，飞行员失去了一些福利，这份工作

sentences.en: became a little bit more of a grind, and it sort of lost a little bit of its luster.
sentences.zh: 变得更像是一场苦差事，并且它多少失去了一些光彩。

sentences.en: And so we end up in this position where there's just not enough people in the pipeline, and suddenly the industry needs a ton of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终陷入了这样一种境地：人才管道里的人根本不够，而航空业突然又需要大量的人。

sentences.en: And so you start to just see airlines desperately doing what they can.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始看到航空公司不顾一切地采取他们能采取的措施。

sentences.en: They're announcing pilot academies.
sentences.zh: 他们正在宣布成立飞行员学院。

sentences.en: They're poaching pilots from smaller carriers.
sentences.zh: 他们从小型航空公司那里挖角飞行员。

sentences.en: And then once you hire all those pilots, you've got to train them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你雇用了所有这些飞行员，你就必须培训他们。

sentences.en: Training has its own bottlenecks.
sentences.zh: 培训本身就有瓶颈。

sentences.en: You can only get retrained on certain aircraft in certain places, so you have to find time to make it to the training center.
sentences.zh: 你只能在特定地点的特定飞机上接受再培训，所以你必须腾出时间前往培训中心。

sentences.en: There has to be class instruction, and with COVID, those classes are smaller.
sentences.zh: 必须有课堂授课，而由于新冠疫情，这些班级的规模变小了。

sentences.en: And so there's just this hiring bottleneck, and then there's this training bottleneck, and they're still working through that part of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里既有招聘瓶颈，又有培训瓶颈，他们仍在努力克服这部分困难。

sentences.en: So I get that there's a lot of people on airplanes that need to be highly trained.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白，飞机上有很多人需要接受高度培训。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, are there other problems outside of the plane itself that are making this worse?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，飞机本身之外是否还有其他问题让情况变得更糟？

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's the second type of labor shortage I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我提到的第二类劳动力短缺。

sentences.en: And this one is affecting airlines, airports, the whole system.
sentences.zh: 而这一问题正在影响航空公司、机场以及整个系统。

sentences.en: Maybe it's helpful to think about what your typical experience at an airport is.
sentences.zh: 思考一下你在机场的典型经历可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Imagine you show up at an airport.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你出现在机场。

sentences.en: You have a bag.
sentences.zh: 你有一个包。

sentences.en: Let's say you want to check that bag.
sentences.zh: 假设你想托运那个包。

sentences.en: You go up to a ticketing agent for your airline.
sentences.zh: 你走到你所乘航空公司的售票代理处。

sentences.en: You hand them the bag.
sentences.zh: 你把包递给他们。

sentences.en: They eventually get the bag into the hands of a baggage handler, and that person gets your bag on the plane.
sentences.zh: 他们最终将包交到行李搬运工手中，那个人把你的包搬上飞机。

sentences.en: While they're doing that, you go to security, and you get screened by a TSA officer.
sentences.zh: 当他们这么做的时候，你去过安检，并接受运输安全管理局官员的筛查。

sentences.en: That's another person in this chain.
sentences.zh: 那是这条链条中的另一个人。

sentences.en: Once you get through there, hopefully it's quick, you get to your gate, and there's a gate agent who might be available to help you if you have any issues.
sentences.zh: 一旦你通过了那里，希望过程很快，你就到了登机口，如果有任何问题，可能会有一名登机口代理人随时为你提供帮助。

sentences.en: Now, while you're sort of waiting to port your plane, you've got caterers, cleaners, mechanics, people on the tarmac, all getting your plane ready for you.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你在等待登机时，你有配餐员、清洁工、机修工、停机坪上的工作人员，所有人都在为你准备飞机。

sentences.en: And then, after all of that, the pilot has to get clearance from air traffic control.
sentences.zh: 然后，在这一切之后，飞行员必须获得空中交通管制部门的许可。

sentences.en: So you can imagine that if at any point along that chain, if they have trouble staffing up, it's going to reverberate, and you're going to be late.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，如果在该链条的任何节点上，他们的人手配备出现问题，就会产生连锁反应，而你就会迟到。

sentences.en: A lot of these jobs are low-wage, and it's a competitive market for those workers.
sentences.zh: 其中许多工作都是低薪的，对于这些工人来说，这是一个竞争激烈的市场。

sentences.en: If you don't feel like working long hours at the airport, or you're getting yelled at by travelers, isn't your idea of fun, you've got other options.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想在机场长时间工作，或者遭到旅客的呵斥不是你认为有趣的想法，你还有别的选择。

sentences.en: So we're seeing the same labor issues afflicting other industries at play here.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到困扰其他行业的劳动力问题在这里也同样存在。

sentences.en: But if staffing is low at a restaurant, you don't get your meal on time.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果餐馆人手不足，你可能无法按时拿到饭菜。

sentences.en: The stakes are obviously so much higher for the airline industry.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，航空业的利害关系要高得多。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, if your pizza is not going to be ready on time, or if they tell you that it's going to be an hour wait, guess what?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你的披萨没能按时做好，或者如果他们告诉你需要等待一个小时，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You can walk down the street to another restaurant.
sentences.zh: 你可以步行到街的另一家餐馆。

sentences.en: You don't have the same option at an airport.
sentences.zh: 你在机场没有同样的选项。

sentences.en: You've already paid.
sentences.zh: 你已经付过钱了。

sentences.en: It may be too late to cancel.
sentences.zh: 现在取消可能已经太晚了。

sentences.en: It may be too frustrating to try to figure out, can you get on a different airline?
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚你是否能换乘另一家航空公司可能会让人太沮丧。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, stakes are way higher.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，利害关系要高得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, just as an example, if your flight gets messed up because of, say, a hurricane, and then you're stuck for hours, seven hours, maybe at an airport,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就拿一个例子来说，如果你的航班因为比如说飓风而被打乱，然后你被困了好几个小时，七个小时，也许是在机场，

sentences.en: because there aren't any pilots that could get you out of town, you may find yourself spending those
sentences.zh: 因为没有任何飞行员能把你带出城，你可能会发现自己把这

sentences.en: seven precious hours of your life studying your seatmates' wedding photos from, like, 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 生命中宝贵的七个小时用来研究你的邻座大约40年前的婚礼照片了。

sentences.en: That sounds awfully specific, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常具体，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It is specifically about me.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是关于我自己的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, joking aside, you mentioned hurricanes, and that actually makes me think of the last major problem that the industry is dealing with.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，抛开玩笑不谈，你提到了飓风，这实际上让我想起了该行业正在处理的最后一个主要问题。

sentences.en: And this one also came out of the pandemic, and that's that travel behavior has changed.
sentences.zh: 这也是从疫情中衍生出来的一个问题，那就是人们的旅行习惯发生了改变。

sentences.en: Take Florida, for example.
sentences.zh: 以佛罗里达州为例。

sentences.en: It's always been really busy.
sentences.zh: 那里一直非常繁忙。

sentences.en: And Florida deals with a lot of storMs. People every summer travel to Miami, to Orlando, but it's only become
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州经常遭遇风暴。每年夏天人们都会去迈阿密、奥兰多，但它变得更加

sentences.en: busier throughout the pandemic because it was one of the few places that you could go where you could stay outside and still feel like you're actually on vacation.
sentences.zh: 繁忙是在疫情期间，因为它是你可以去的少数几个能够待在户外并且仍然觉得自己在度假的地方之一。

sentences.en: And it continues to be a really popular destination.
sentences.zh: 而且它依然是一个非常热门的目的地。

sentences.en: And what you see is people are flying to different places than they were before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的是，人们飞往的地方与疫情前不同了。

sentences.en: They're flying for different durations.
sentences.zh: 他们的飞行时长不同了。

sentences.en: They're flying on different days.
sentences.zh: 他们在不同的日子飞行。

sentences.en: And that's placed more of an emphasis on things working right in those places that they're going to.
sentences.zh: 这就更加强调了他们要去的地方一切都要正常运转。

sentences.en: And when they don't, like when there's a hurricane in Florida, it creates a problem that can reverberate throughout the system.
sentences.zh: 当它们不正常运转时，比如佛罗里达州发生飓风，就会产生一个可能在整个系统中产生连锁反应的问题。

sentences.en: And the industry has to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 而该行业必须应对这一点。

sentences.en: And what they've done is something that makes a lot of economic sense, but it also sort of complicates the problem, right?
sentences.zh: 他们所做的事情在经济上非常有意义，但这也使问题在某种程度上变得更加复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: They basically said, we realize we stretch ourselves too thin.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是说，我们意识到我们的步子迈得太大、人手拉得太薄了。

sentences.en: We're going to actually not offer as many flights as we had hoped and as the demand supports.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上不打算提供原本希望提供的那么多航班，也不提供需求所支持的那么多航班。

sentences.en: And in one way, that's great.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这很好。

sentences.en: It means that they have extra pilots, extra planes, extra flight attendants, et cetera, to deal with any probleMs. But on the other hand, it means that
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们有额外的飞行员、额外的飞机、额外的乘务员等来处理任何问题。但另一方面，这意味着

sentences.en: if there are problems, there aren't a lot of options for customers to rebook or to kind of look elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 如果出现问题，客户改签或寻找其他选择的余地并不多。

sentences.en: And so it's a little bit of a catch-22.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像一个进退维谷的困境。

sentences.en: What you're saying is in order to solve this problem of delays and cancellations, the airline's main strategy has been to cut back on flights.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，为了解决航班延误和取消的问题，航空公司的主要策略一直是削减航班。

sentences.en: That does strike me as kind of counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 这确实让我觉得有点适得其反。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I mean, in the short term, it's the move that's serving the industry beSt. But if you're a
sentences.zh: 是的，但我的意思是，在短期内，这是对该行业最有利的举措。但如果你是一个

sentences.en: passenger, flights are more expensive, there are fewer options, and you're left wondering who to blame.
sentences.zh: 乘客，机票更贵了，选择更少了，你只能纳闷该怪谁。

sentences.en: Neeraj, you've laid out the reasons behind the nightmare that so many of us have experienced.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，你列举了我们当中许多人所经历的这场噩梦背后的原因。

sentences.en: But didn't we kind of pay to fix this already as taxpayers with that bailout?
sentences.zh: 但我们难道不是作为纳税人通过那笔救助金已经花钱解决了这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't that have bought us a more functional summer of travel?
sentences.zh: 那难道不应该为我们买到一个更加顺畅的夏季旅行季吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think a lot of people would argue that it did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为很多人会争辩说确实如此。

sentences.en: If airlines didn't get that money, they would have been allowed to make much deeper cuts, and some could have even risked bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 如果航空公司没有拿到这笔钱，他们就会被允许进行更大幅度的削减，其中一些甚至可能面临破产的风险。

sentences.en: And so this might just be the best summer we could have hoped for.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能已经是我们可以希望的最好的夏天了。

sentences.en: That is dark.
sentences.zh: 真黑暗。

sentences.en: It is, but maybe looking at the numbers will make you feel a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但也许看看数字会让你感觉好一点。

sentences.en: So look, this summer is bad.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，今年夏天很糟糕。

sentences.en: Flight cancellations, flight delays are both up by about a third from the summer of 2019.
sentences.zh: 航班取消和航班延误都比2019年夏天增加了大约三分之一。

sentences.en: But if you look at the actual hard numbers, in 2019, just under two out of every
sentences.zh: 但如果你看实际的确切数字，在2019年，每

sentences.en: 100 flights was canceled.
sentences.zh: 100个航班中只有不到2个被取消。

sentences.en: This time around, it's just over two.
sentences.zh: 这一次，数字刚刚超过2个。

sentences.en: That's still a pretty small share.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个相当小的比例。

sentences.en: When it comes to delays, about 19% of flights are delayed in 2019.
sentences.zh: 至于延误，2019年大约有19%的航班延误。

sentences.en: This year, it's up to about 24%.
sentences.zh: 今年，这一比例上升到了大约24%。

sentences.en: So it is worse.
sentences.zh: 所以情况确实更糟糕了。

sentences.en: But, you know, this is kind of looking like a bad summer, but not a drastically bad summer.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这看起来像是一个糟糕的夏天，但并不是一个极其糟糕的夏天。

sentences.en: But why does it feel so much worse, then?
sentences.zh: 那为什么感觉糟糕得多呢？

sentences.en: To some extent, it might be perception.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这可能是一种感知问题。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of us haven't been on any big trips throughout the pandemic, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们中的许多人在整个疫情期间都没有进行过任何大型旅行，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I went to Sweden last month, and I put so much pressure on that trip, because I'd been really missing traveling abroad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我上个月去了瑞典，我对那次旅行寄予了厚望，因为我真的很想念出国旅行。

sentences.en: And it was such an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多么好的机会啊。

sentences.en: And I was lucky.
sentences.zh: 而且我很幸运。

sentences.en: It wasn't too bad.
sentences.zh: 情况不算太糟。

sentences.en: I had one missed connection, but it only delayed me by a few hours.
sentences.zh: 我有一次转机没赶上，但这只让我耽误了几个小时。

sentences.en: But, you know, in some cases, it can be one, two days.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在某些情况下，可能会耽误一天、两天。

sentences.en: I mean, you can miss a wedding.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能会错过一场婚礼。

sentences.en: You know, after a pandemic where you've been sort of locked into your local area, there's a lot riding on these.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在经历了把你局限在本地的疫情之后，这些事情的赌注很高。

sentences.en: You're saying, in one sense, the problem is that our expectations might just be too high,
sentences.zh: 你是说，从某种意义上说，问题在于我们的期望可能太高了，

sentences.en: which I get, but is also a hard pill to swallow just because I'm paying so much more for flights.
sentences.zh: 我能理解这一点，但这也是一个很难接受的事实，仅仅因为我为机票支付了高得多的费用。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: It is more expensive.
sentences.zh: 确实更贵了。

sentences.en: Fares are up double-digit percentage from 2019.
sentences.zh: 票价比2019年呈两位数百分比增长。

sentences.en: And, you know, on one hand, the biggest airlines just reported record revenue in this last quarter, but they've also spent a lot of that money.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一方面，最大的几家航空公司刚刚报告了上一季度创纪录的收入，但他们也花了很多钱。

sentences.en: And so if you look at profits, what they've actually kept, they've reported profits, which is great, coming out of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看利润，他们实际保留下来的部分，他们报告了利润，这很棒，走出了疫情的阴影。

sentences.en: That hasn't happened for a while.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经有一段时间没有发生了。

sentences.en: But they've been spending a lot of money on jet fuel, a lot of money on everything from food to, as we've discussed, labor.
sentences.zh: 但他们一直在喷气燃料上花很多钱，在从食品到正如我们所讨论的劳动力等方方面面花很多钱。

sentences.en: Neeraj, you said you were going to make me feel better, but I am not feeling better right now.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，你说过你要让我感觉好一点，但我现在一点也没觉得好受。

sentences.en: How does this interminable mess of it all end?
sentences.zh: 这一切没完没了的混乱将如何结束？

sentences.en: Well, so there are a few ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以有几种方式。

sentences.en: Lawmakers have proposed a bill that would make it harder for airlines to offer a schedule that they can't staff.
sentences.zh: 议员们提出了一项法案，该法案将使航空公司更难以提供他们无法配备人手的航班时刻表。

sentences.en: So if they know they don't have the staffing, they just wouldn't be allowed to put it out there.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他们知道自己人手不足，他们将根本不被允许将其发布出来。

sentences.en: At the same time, the transportation department is looking to kind of harden the rules around consumer protections.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，交通部正着手加强围绕消费者保护的规则。

sentences.en: They want to make it easier for you to get a refund, harder for airlines to push you towards taking credit for a refund.
sentences.zh: 他们希望让你更容易获得退款，让航空公司更难强迫你接受退款信用额度。

sentences.en: And then the other thing is that the summer's winding down.
sentences.zh: 然后另一件事是夏天即将过去。

sentences.en: Fall is always a slower season.
sentences.zh: 秋天历来是一个较慢的季节。

sentences.en: So airlines might have a little bit of breathing room soon to sort things out.
sentences.zh: 因此航空公司很快可能会有一些喘息的空间来收拾残局。

sentences.en: You're saying we're already maybe through the worst of this?
sentences.zh: 你是说我们可能已经度过了最艰难的时期？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: July was a really busy month, but we're halfway through AuguSt. And, you know, kids are going to go back to school.
sentences.zh: 七月是个非常忙碌的月份，但八月已经过半了。而且，你知道的，孩子们就要返校了。

sentences.en: People are going to get back to work.
sentences.zh: 人们要回去上班了。

sentences.en: And, you know, fewer people are going to fly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，坐飞机的人会变少。

sentences.en: There's a light at the end of the tunnel here.
sentences.zh: 这里终于看到了一线曙光。

sentences.en: A single on-time flight in our future?
sentences.zh: 我们未来能坐上一趟准点航班吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's hard to predict, but it's possible that we see a return to normal next summer.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很难预测，但我们有可能在明年夏天恢复正常。

sentences.en: But keep in mind that normal isn't always that great.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，正常并不总是那么美好。

sentences.en: You know, still means delays, still means canceled flights, but it could at least be better than this summer.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那仍然意味着延误，仍然意味着航班取消，但至少可能会比今年夏天好一些。

sentences.en: Neeraj, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 尼拉杰，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: Tonight, Harriet Hageman has received the most votes in this primary.
sentences.zh: 今晚，哈丽特·哈吉曼在这次初选中获得了最多的选票。

sentences.en: She won.
sentences.zh: 她赢了。

sentences.en: I called her to concede the race.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给她承认了竞选失败。

sentences.en: This primary election is over.
sentences.zh: 这场初选已经结束了。

sentences.en: Congresswoman Liz Cheney of Wyoming, who alienated both her Republican colleagues and her constituents by demanding that Donald Trump be
sentences.zh: 怀俄明州国会女议员莉兹·切尼因要求唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: held accountable for his role in the January 6th attack on the Capitol, was defeated on Tuesday in a Republican primary.
sentences.zh: 对其在1月6日国会山袭击事件中所扮演的角色承担责任，从而疏远了她的共和党同僚和选民，她在周二的共和党初选中落败。

sentences.en: Cheney was beaten by an opponent, Harriet Hageman, who falsely claims that the 2020 election was rigged and who was endorsed by Trump.
sentences.zh: 切尼被她的对手哈丽特·哈吉曼击败，后者曾虚假宣称2020年大选被操纵，并得到了特朗普的支持。

sentences.en: Cheney was widely expected to lose after bucking her party's leadership, first by voting to impeach Trump in 2021, and then by becoming an
sentences.zh: 外界普遍预计切尼会输，因为她先是在2021年投票弹劾特朗普，随后又成为

sentences.en: outspoken member of the House committee investigating January 6th.
sentences.zh: 调查1月6日事件众议院委员会中直言不讳的成员，从而违背了党内领导层的意愿。

sentences.en: She becomes the latest House Republican to pay a political price for crossing Trump.
sentences.zh: 她成为了又一位因冒犯特朗普而付出政治代价的众议院共和党人。

sentences.en: So far, of the 10 House Republicans who voted to impeach him over January 6th, eight have either lost re-election or said they would resign.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，在因1月6日事件投票弹劾特朗普的10名众议院共和党人中，已有8人要么在连任竞选中落败，要么宣布辞职。

sentences.en: Two years ago, I won this primary with 73% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 两年前，我以73%的得票率赢得了这场初选。

sentences.en: I could easily have done the same again.
sentences.zh: 我本可以轻而易举地再次做到这一点。

sentences.en: The path was clear.
sentences.zh: 道路是清晰的。

sentences.en: But it would have required that I go along with President Trump's lie about the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 但这需要我附和特朗普总统关于2020年大选的谎言。

sentences.en: It would have required that I enable his ongoing efforts to unravel our democratic system and attack the foundations of our republic.
sentences.zh: 这需要我纵容他不断试图瓦解我们民主制度并攻击我们共和国基石的行为。

sentences.en: That was a path I could not and would not take.
sentences.zh: 那是我不能也不会走的路。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Nina Feldman, Luke Vanderplug, and Sydney Harper.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由妮娜·费尔德曼、卢克·范德普鲁格和悉尼·哈珀制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by
sentences.zh: 节目剪辑自

sentences.en: John Ketchum and M.J.
sentences.zh: 约翰·凯彻姆和M·J·

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, contains original music by Marion Lozano, Dan Powell, and was engineered by Corey Schreppel.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯·林恩，原创音乐由马里昂·洛扎诺、丹·鲍威尔创作，并由科里·施雷佩尔进行混音工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansworth of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯沃斯创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗韦斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您准备节日期间的待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是一觉睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有食物过敏或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》App上或您习惯收听播客的任何地方找到《Wirecutter秀》。
